rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.3-2.5 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own case study on a 3.3 ha Verdicchio plot in Marche (airborne thermal surveys in June/July/August 2021, Bioristor in vivo sensors with Sentek multilevel soil probes over 150 days, questionnaire-based cost data, WP/EWP indices).
rows.notes: The study is a prototype description and case study in a vineyard that has no irrigation system (Section 2.1; Conclusions list this as a limitation). Soil moisture probes (Sentek) are used only to log soil water content and to compare with Bioristor response (Section 3.3, Figure 10); they are never used to schedule or optimise irrigation, and no water saving or water-use-efficiency outcome attributable to sensor use is measured. WP figures in Table 4 compare an unirrigated 2020 season with a hypothetical/estimated irrigated 2021 scenario (costs taken from a neighbouring plot, yield estimated), and WP actually falls under the irrigation scenario. The study therefore only shows that sensors can monitor/detect vine water stress (a precondition of the claimed optimisation), not that soil sensors deliver water use efficiency. Most of the sensing results concern thermal CWSI maps and the Bioristor rather than soil sensors.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.3-2.5 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own measurements (thermal surveys, Bioristor and soil-probe monitoring, farm cost questionnaire, yields in Table 3) from a single pilot vineyard in Serra De' Conti, Italy.
rows.notes: No measured effect of soil sensors (or any sensor) on grape yield or quality is reported. The plot was not irrigated; the 2021 real yield was 86 q/ha due to drought, and the 103 q/ha figure 'with irrigation' in Table 3 is an estimate assuming the winery had irrigated in response to sensor-detected stress, not an observed result. Grape quality was not measured. The study shows only that sensors (mainly Bioristor and thermal CWSI, with soil probes as ancillary) detected drought stress during flowering and veraison, which is a precondition for the claimed yield/quality maintenance rather than evidence of it. The authors themselves note the absence of a precision irrigation system as a limitation of the study as a whole.

notes: Full text appears complete (Sections 1-4, tables, references). The paper is a descriptive single-site case study of an IoT platform prototype combining airborne thermal CWSI, an in vivo Bioristor biosensor, Sentek soil probes and an economic simulation; it reports uncertainty only for canopy temperature/CWSI distributions (Table 1), not for any irrigation outcome. Soil sensors are a minor component, and irrigation was never applied on the studied plot, so neither claim is supported by the study's own results.
